card: Suspends the 20-minute ping timeout for peers actively serving blocks during block download, providing a one-minute grace period after the last block is received. This resolves #35761, where downloading nodes with slow bandwidth mistakenly disconnect healthy peers that prioritize queued block delivery ahead of pongs. Block download stalling, inactivity, and peer-download timeouts remain in effect to catch dead connections.
changed_since_previous: No functional logic changes; the patch-id changed, likely from rebasing or test adjustments.
evidence: Fixes #35761 ('Unnecessary disconnections due to PONG delays during the initial block download')

Author note in PR description: 'if we do IBD with a low download bandwidth (that is distributed over 10 peers) a peer will not get around to answering our ping before the timeout of 20 minutes, in which case we would disconnect them, although they have done nothing wrong and are not even slow themselves (we are).'
problem: During initial block download on constrained bandwidth, peers prioritize block transmission over responding to pings. This causes downloading nodes to disconnect fast, well-behaved peers after a 20-minute ping timeout simply because the downloader cannot process block data fast enough to receive the peer's pong.

risk.why: Modifies peer timeout and disconnection criteria in P2P message processing, which could risk leaving unresponsive or malicious peers connected longer than intended if the conditions are flawed.

summary: This PR moves the ping timeout check from `MaybeSendPing` into `SendMessages` and suspends ping timeouts for any peer that currently has blocks in flight, adding a one-minute grace period after the last block is received. It includes functional test coverage verifying both the delayed pong behavior during IBD and the suspended ping timeout logic.
